items.title: Bitcoin's 'Lost' Wallets Weren't Actually Lost
points: A 2018 analysis tracked 92,076 Bitcoin wallets inactive for 6+ years; revisiting the list in 2026 found 9,990 wallets had moved 245,000 BTC ($14.7 billion) total.

A New York lawsuit seeks to declare 39,069 dormant addresses (including wallets linked to Bitcoin creator Satoshi Nakamoto) as abandoned property, but blockchain records show some have already moved funds and one holder has filed to dismiss.

The blockchain (public ledger recording all transactions, but not account holder identities) only shows inactivity, not whether funds are truly lost—someone could move coins without revealing who they are.
Findings suggest many 'lost' coins were simply held by inactive owners rather than permanently lost to forgotten keys or deleted files.

items.title: Law Enforcement Tracks Stolen Crypto Across Multiple Crimes
points: The U.S. Justice Department is forfeiting $1.1 billion in USDC (a U.S. dollar-pegged stablecoin) from the October 2024 Binance hack attributed to North Korean actors, bringing total recovered/frozen crypto from that theft to $2.9 billion.
Europol coordinated with police in 11 countries, plus Binance, Coinbase, and blockchain analysis firm Chainalysis, to trace $28 million in crypto payments funding Europe's illegal streaming services.
These operations highlight growing sophistication in tracing crypto transactions to crime, even as bad actors seek new ways to move stolen funds.

items.title: Gold Prices Slide
points: Gold prices fell to 16-month lows below $3,600.
Market predictions now give a 52% chance gold drops to $3,500 by November 30.

items.title: CFTC Bitcoin Reserves Ruling
points: CFTC (Commodity Futures Trading Commission—the U.S. regulator overseeing derivatives exchanges) staff guidance now allows regulated exchanges and clearinghouses to count bitcoin holdings toward mandatory financial reserve requirements.
The change recognizes bitcoin as a viable asset class for regulatory capital purposes, lowering barriers for exchanges to hold it as backup liquidity.
Could boost institutional adoption by making bitcoin reserves more economically attractive than traditional reserve assets for trading platforms.

items.title: UniCredit Bitcoin Product Launch
points: Italy's UniCredit bank launched a structured investment product linked to bitcoin with 100% capital protection, meaning investors cannot lose their initial deposit regardless of price moves.
The product caps upside potential in exchange for guaranteeing return of principal, targeting risk-averse retail investors.
Signals a major European bank's confidence in crypto market maturity and demand for regulated, principal-protected crypto exposure.

issues.subject: 👀 CFTC Lets Regulated Exchanges Count Bitcoin Toward Required Reserves

headlines: CFTC staff approves bitcoin as eligible collateral for regulated futures exchanges and clearinghouses to meet financial reserve requirements, expanding institutional crypto integration.
Italy's UniCredit bank launches bitcoin-linked structured product offering 100% capital protection, signaling mainstream financial institution appetite for crypto exposure.

sections.title: CFTC Bitcoin Reserves Ruling
points: CFTC (Commodity Futures Trading Commission—the U.S. regulator overseeing derivatives exchanges) staff guidance allows regulated exchanges and clearinghouses to count bitcoin holdings toward their mandatory financial resources reserves.
This change recognizes bitcoin as a viable asset class for meeting regulatory capital requirements, reducing barriers for exchanges to hold crypto as backup liquidity.
The ruling could increase institutional adoption by making it economically attractive for trading platforms to maintain bitcoin reserves rather than other traditional assets.

sections.title: UniCredit Bitcoin Product Launch
points: Italy's UniCredit bank introduced a structured investment product linked to bitcoin with 100% capital protection—meaning investors cannot lose their initial deposit regardless of bitcoin price movements.
The product caps upside potential while guaranteeing principal return, appealing to risk-averse retail investors seeking bitcoin exposure without downside volatility risk.
Launch reflects major European bank's confidence in crypto market maturity and demand for regulated, principal-protected instruments among traditional banking customers.
